params.text: Sermilik Fjord and Helheim Glacier, SE Greenland
glacier ice flows to the sea
calving front (terminus): the ice face in (c) and (d)
ice mélange: icebergs and sea ice
Imagery: NASA Worldview / GIBS. (a) MODIS Terra true colour, 5 Aug 2022. (b) Harmonized Landsat Sentinel-2 (HLS S30), 30 Jul 2022; contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data 2022.
(c) is a schematic: not to scale; the plume and icebergs are enlarged.
Processes at a tidewater glacier and in its fjord
subglacial discharge: meltwater drains via moulins to channels at the bed, exits at the grounding line
buoyant plume: rises along the ice; eddies on its edge engulf ambient water (entrainment)
submarine melting: the plume carries heat to the ice face
neutral buoyancy: the plume detaches and flows out toward the sea
warm Atlantic Water flows toward the glacier at depth, replacing the entrained water
along-fjord wind drives an exchange with the shelf
shelf forcing: the pycnocline heaves over days and the motion enters the fjord
Plume geometry at the ice face: configurations (a) and (b)
q0 per metre of ice face (2-D)
configuration (a): a line plume, discharge along the whole face
configuration (b): two point plumes, x0 apart
